macros.name: derivskip
macros.doc: The default space (8pt) between lines in a derivation.

macros.name: done
macros.doc: The \done command (\done[⟨number⟩]) can be used to close a assumption and/or introduction without mentioning why.

macros.name: done
macros.doc: The \done command (\done[⟨number⟩]) can be used to close a assumption and/or introduction without mentioning why.

macros.name: inlcmnts
macros.doc: Command to switch inline comments explicitly on (and by that, overriding and forgetting the default determined by the absence or presence of the inlcmnts package option).

macros.name: introsymb
macros.doc: The symbol used as variable introduction prefix.

macros.name: noinlcmnts
macros.doc: Command to switch inline comments explicitly off (and by that, overriding and forgetting the default determined by the absence or presence of the inlcmnts package option).

macros.name: skipsteps*
macros.doc: For skipping an unknown number of steps in a manual numbered derivation, the command \skipsteps*{⟨formula⟩}{⟨comment⟩} can be used.

macros.name: theinlcmnt
macros.doc: The command used to format inline comments (if enabled).

macros.name: thestepcount
macros.doc: This is the command used to generate a step number label (used by autonumbering).

macros.name: thesteplabel
macros.doc: Command used to generate a customized step label (used by manual numbering).

envs.name: flagderiv
envs.doc: Basic derivations are written using an intuitive command sequence placed in the flagderiv environment.

envs.name: flagderiv
envs.doc: Basic derivations are written using an intuitive command sequence placed in the flagderiv environment.

envs.name: flagderiv*
envs.doc: The flagderiv* environment is almost the same as flagderiv with the only difference that the resulting derivation will and can not be split across pages.
